change.title: @google/generative-ai (npm) is deprecated and reaches end of life; migrate to @google/genai

source.quote: All support for this repository (including bug fixes) will permanently end on **November 30, 2025**.

tasks.reasoning:
The repo depends on @google/generative-ai 0.24.1 according to package-lock.json, and that version falls in the EOL range (<=0.24.1). Support, including bug fixes, ended permanently on 2025-11-30, so the repo is already past the deadline. It now runs an unmaintained SDK that will not receive fixes for new API behaviour or models. The migration is to @google/genai at the current version: replace the dependency, rewrite the client construction and the getGenerativeModel call site, and update the response handling. The scan did not read the response handling, so the migration agent should check how the response text is read (response.text() becomes response.text) and any chat/history usage.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- gemini:genai-js-0x-breaking-0-9-0 (sdk-major): @google/genai (npm) 0.9.0 (0.x): generateContent contents parameter types simplified (also 0.7.0 File.sizeBytes number to string, 0.5.0 turnComplete default true, 0.3.0 file.upload named params), effective 2025-04-17. The early @google/genai 0.x changes, such as the simplified generateContent contents types, only matter once the repo moves to @google/genai. The migration should target the current release and write contents in the current simplified form, so no separate edit is needed.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googleapis/js-genai/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "Simplified the types allowed on the generateContent contents parameter."

callSites.why: Uses getGenerativeModel({ model, systemInstruction }) from @google/generative-ai 0.24.1, the deprecated package whose support ended 2025-11-30. It must be rewritten for @google/genai: new GoogleGenAI client, ai.models.generateContent / ai.chats.create, and systemInstruction moved into config.
The model string gemini-2.5-flash-lite should carry over unchanged into the new SDK's model parameter.

record.prBody:
## @google/generative-ai (npm) is deprecated and reaches end of life; migrate to @google/genai [Verified]

### Change

Replaced @google/generative-ai with @google/genai (^2.32.0) via npm. In src/services/gemini.js: `new GoogleGenAI({apiKey})`, and `getGenerativeModel` + `model.generateContent` became `ai.models.generateContent({model, contents, config:{systemInstruction}})`. Response text is now read from the `result.text` getter (string) instead of `text()`. The contents are a plain string, which is the current simplified form (this covers the genai 0.9.0 contents change). Added scripts/check-genai.mjs as the proof test.

Files touched:
- `package-lock.json`
- `package.json`
- `scripts/check-genai.mjs`
- `src/services/gemini.js`

### Why

@google/generative-ai is EOL (support ended 2025-11-30). The new SDK has a different client, a different call shape and a different response shape.

> All support for this repository (including bug fixes) will permanently end on **November 30, 2025**.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/generative-ai-js/HEAD/README.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| build | pass | pass | 0 |
| genai-proof | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- genai-proof, added by the agent: `node scripts/check-genai.mjs` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Test of this change: `genai-proof`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- Live response shape not exercised
- @google/genai 2.x requires Node >=20; engines and CI were not checked
- Vite bundling of @google/genai in the browser was only checked by the build passing
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- The old SDK's `result.text` was undefined, so the code fell through to the nested-response branch. It now takes the `result.text` string directly. Empty or blocked responses are no longer thrown by text(); they fall through to the candidates branch or an empty or JSON result.
- Node >=20 is required by @google/genai.

---

preparation.reasoning: A plain Vite + React app: `vite build` needs no codegen, no workspace package builds, and no env vars at build time. The package.json has no postinstall, prepare or generate scripts, so nothing was skipped by installing with scripts off.

review.summary: The one call site in src/services/gemini.js is migrated cleanly to the new SDK shape: `new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey })`, then `genAI.models.generateContent({ model, contents, config: { systemInstruction } })`, with the response read via `result.text` as a string. One detail worth knowing: the old code's `typeof result.text === "function"` branch never matched, because the old SDK put `text()` on `result.response`, so it always fell through to the `result.response?.candidates` branch. The build only proves the import resolves and Vite bundles it. genai-proof is a regex script the agent wrote itself, checking for the absence of old identifiers and the presence of `models.generateContent(`. Nothing exercises a real or mocked call, the response parsing, or the 429 fallback path. "Verified" leans heavily on a self-authored grep. I could not confirm `@google/genai` 2.32.0 or `@types/node` 26.6.6 from memory; the lockfile and the npm registry are where to check.

concerns.issue: The 429 fallback relies on `error.message?.includes("429") || error.status === 429`. The new SDK throws a different error class than the old `GoogleGenerativeAIFetchError`. It likely exposes `status`, but no check exercises it, and a mismatch would silently send rate-limited users to the generic 'technical difficulties' fallback.

The agent-authored proof only greps the source and package.json. It does not show that the request shape (`contents` as a string, `config.systemInstruction`) is accepted at runtime or that `result.text` is populated. It is not wired into package.json scripts, so it becomes stray repo clutter unless kept on purpose.

`@google/genai` declares `engines.node >=20.0.0`, up from `>=18` for the old package. Any CI or deploy image still on Node 18 may warn or fail installs. The package also pulls in Node-oriented dependencies (google-auth-library, ws, protobufjs) for what is a browser bundle. The build passed, but check bundle size and confirm the browser entry point is the one being resolved.

I could not confirm from memory that `@google/genai` ^2.32.0 exists as a published version with the `models.generateContent` and `.text` getter API. Check it against the npm registry and the SDK's shipped type definitions.

checkFirst: Run the app with a real VITE_GEMINI_API_KEY and send one message. Confirm the reply comes from `result.text` and includes the system-instruction disclaimer, which shows `config.systemInstruction` is honoured.
Force or mock a 429 from the new SDK and confirm `error.status === 429` (or the message check) still routes to the rate-limit fallback text.
Confirm the deploy/CI Node version is >= 20 and check the Vite bundle size change after adding @google/genai.
Decide whether to keep scripts/check-genai.mjs in the repo, and consider grading this needs-review, since no check makes a live or mocked API call.

source.quote:
now store requests by default
(`store=true`), matching the Interactions API.

tasks.reasoning: From 2026-10-26, new paid-tier projects store Generate Content requests by default (store=true). The repo is a healthcare bot, so stored prompts may contain sensitive health data. It is uncertain whether this project's API key belongs to a new paid-tier project, so the migration agent should check. If it does, or to be safe, pass store=false on generateContent calls, which likely requires the @google/genai SDK. This needs its own edit beyond the SDK migration, so it is kept as a separate task.

## Generate Content API: new paid-tier projects now store requests by default (store=true); opt out with store=false [Verified]

### Change

Ported src/services/gemini.js from the deprecated @google/generative-ai to @google/genai 2.32.0 (npm). The call is now ai.models.generateContent with config.store=false and systemInstruction under config. Added scripts/check-store.mjs as the proof check.

Files touched:
- `package-lock.json`
- `package.json`
- `scripts/check-store.mjs`
- `src/services/gemini.js`

### Why

Changelog: new paid-tier projects store generateContent requests by default (store=true). This is a healthcare bot, so the request sets store=false. The old SDK has no store field, so it had to be replaced. @google/genai 2.32.0 types store in GenerateContentConfig.

> now store requests by default
> (`store=true`), matching the Interactions API.

Source: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/changelog.md.txt

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| build | pass | pass | 0 |
| store-proof | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- store-proof, added by the agent: `node scripts/check-store.mjs` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Test of this change: `store-proof`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- No live call: the API's acceptance of store:false is unconfirmed.
- Whether this project is a new paid-tier project is unknown. store:false is sent either way.
- @google/genai 2.x needs Node >=20; engines and CI were not checked.
- The proof script is a static check that the text exists. It does not show the field reaches the wire.
- The key is read from VITE_GEMINI_API_KEY and used in the browser. The repo had this before the change.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- The new SDK result has a text getter, not a function, so the existing fallback chain reads candidates instead. The output should be the same.
- Any error, including an API rejection of store, falls through to the local fallback text. The fallback never calls the API, so it never sends store.
- The request now sends store:false, so it will not be stored.

---

review.summary: The diff moves the one call site (src/services/gemini.js:50) from the legacy @google/generative-ai SDK to @google/genai and passes `store: false` in `config`. That is the right intent for a health app. But the store-proof check only greps the source for the string `store: false`. Nothing shows the option reaches the request body. The PR also swaps the SDK, which is much broader than the API change requires. I don't think 'verified' is earned. The response-parsing path and the opt-out on the wire are both unproven.

concerns.issue: I could not confirm that `GenerateContentConfig` in @google/genai@2.32.0 has a `store` field, or that the SDK serialises it into the generateContent request. The @google/genai SDK maps config fields to the REST body explicitly. If `store` is not in its converter, it may be dropped silently and requests would still be stored by default. That would defeat the whole point for health data. Check the SDK's types (`node_modules/@google/genai/dist/genai.d.ts`) and its request converters, or capture one live request.

The 'store-proof' check is a regex over source text: no `generative-ai`, has `models.generateContent(`, has `store: false`. It proves neither that the SDK accepts the option nor that the API honours it. It also does not show that any call returns a usable response. Passing it does not justify a 'verified' grade.

The response normalisation below the call was not updated. In @google/genai, `result.text` is a getter that returns a string, not a function, so the first branch is skipped. The code then relies on the `result.candidates` branch. That probably works, but it now joins every part, possibly including thought parts. It is untested. If it breaks, the outer try/catch quietly returns canned fallback text, which would hide the regression.

The PR replaces the whole SDK (@google/generative-ai 0.24 → @google/genai ^2.32.0). That goes beyond adding an opt-out flag. The new package requires Node >=20 (the old one needed >=18) and pulls in google-auth-library, ws and protobufjs. This is a Vite browser app, so the client bundle may grow and the browser entry has to resolve correctly. I could not confirm version 2.32.0; check it against npm. The build passing shows it bundles, not that it runs in the browser.
`debug` and `ms` lose their `dev: true` flag and become production dependencies through https-proxy-agent. This is minor, but it is part of the broader dependency change.

This predates the PR, but the API key is still read from VITE_GEMINI_API_KEY and used in the browser. Data-retention settings matter less when the key itself is exposed client-side; it is worth flagging next to a privacy-motivated change.
